patient_answer: Amoxicillin is an antibacterial prescription medicine used to treat common bacterial infections (such as throat, ear, or chest infections).
Take with or after food with a full glass of water at evenly spaced intervals as prescribed.
Finish the ENTIRE course prescribed by your physician, even if you feel better after a few days, to prevent antibiotic resistance.
Inform your doctor immediately if you develop skin rash, itching, lip swelling, or difficulty breathing (signs of penicillin allergy).

doctor_answer.assessment: Moderate-spectrum bactericidal aminopenicillin (WHO AWaRe 'Access' Group). Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis.
doctor_answer.investigations: Verify absence of penicillin or beta-lactam hypersensitivity. Culture & sensitivity testing when indicated.
doctor_answer.management: Adult dosage: 500 mg PO TID or 875-1000 mg PO BID depending on severity. Pediatric: 25-50 mg/kg/day in divided doses. Dose reduce in severe renal insufficiency (eGFR <30 mL/min).
references: WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (23rd List, 2023)

staff_answer: Confirm patient allergy history for penicillins before administration. Observe for 30 minutes following first dose for hypersensitivity.
red_flags: Severe watery diarrhea containing blood or mucus (Clostridioides difficile colitis)
follow_up_questions: Have you ever had an allergic reaction to penicillin or augmentin?
Are you currently pregnant or nursing?
avoid: Do NOT use for viral colds, flu, or simple viral coughs
Do NOT discontinue early when symptoms ease
source: WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (WHO EML) & AWaRe Classification
